summary: This pass expands the public-company universe around qualified non-Chinese strategic-mineral inputs, rare-earth separation, magnet capacity, graphite/anode material, and defense-stockpile supply. The strongest evidence points to a policy-created qualification bottleneck: compliant feedstock, oxide separation, magnet qualification, smelting purity, and customer/offtake certification may matter more than headline mining tonnage. The two-lane result keeps MP Materials as the obvious reference anchor, while the underfollowed lane highlights Energy Fuels, United States Antimony, and Nouveau Monde Graphite as smaller public names with plausible exposure to regulated critical-mineral supply constraints.
